chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter."
He عليه السلام said: "It is Allah's pleasure and Paradise in the Hereafter, and abundance in sustenance and livelihoods, and good character in this world."

key_terms.الرِّزْقِ: sustenance and provision granted by Allah
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the life to come after death
key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise as the ultimate reward in the Hereafter
key_terms.الْمَعَايِشِ: means of living and livelihood conditions
key_terms.رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ: Allah's pleasure and acceptance in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What does "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter" mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the meaning of the supplication asking for good in this world and the Hereafter. The good of the Hereafter is Allah's pleasure and Paradise, while the good of this world is expansive sustenance, ease in livelihood, and noble character. It presents worldly and otherworldly well-being as joined together in a believer's du'a.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3566 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah (as):
Regarding the words of Allah (swt), the Almighty:
"Our Lord (azj), grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201)

Imam (as) said:
"Good in the Hereafter" refers to Allah's (swt) pleasure and Paradise,
and "good in this world" refers to abundance in sustenance, favorable living conditions, and good character.
